call1_AB.raw:
Both fortunes hit criterion 1 squarely — a liquidated trader and a loss in the cookie voice. Criterion 2 is where they part: B's joke lands right on the wound, the fantasy of a windfall collapsing into your own deposit coming back as a margin call is rueful and specific to exactly what just happened. A's "order takeout" is charming and self-aware, but the punchline is a generic food joke rather than one aimed at the loss itself. Criterion 4 confirms it: B's double meaning (windfall = your own money, weaponized) is a genuine turn, while A's three-part structure resolves into the most familiar comfort-food fallback. Both keep the oracular voice and break it cleanly, but B's oracle ("the stars say a windfall is coming") sets up a crueler, funnier swerve.

Verdict: B, margin 2.
call1_AB.reasoning_tail:
Weigh criteria. Both are fortune cookie lines for a liquidated crypto trader.

A: "Your horoscope says: hold. Your portfolio says: sold. The cookie says: order takeout." — trader + loss present, cookie voice, joke is takeout (self-referential, break the fourth wall). Word count: 14. Fresh-ish turn.

B: "The stars say a windfall is coming — it is your own deposit, returning as a margin call." — 18 words, strong joke: windfall double meaning, own deposit returning as margin call. Oracle voice "The stars say" broken by punchline. Very on-point for liquidation (margin call). Fresh, surprising last word.

Both read whole. B's joke lands more sharply on the loss — the windfall being your own money coming back as a margin call is rueful, warm-ish, self-deprecating. A's takeout joke is cute but the "order takeout" break is more generic. B's double meaning is fresher.

Criterion 1: both meet. 2: both laugh-worthy; B lands harder on the loss. 4: B's turn is better. Verdict B, margin 2.

call2_BA.raw:
Both fortunes hit the brief: trader, loss, cookie voice. B's triple rhythm ("hold / sold / takeout") lands but it's a familiar list-gag shape, and "sold" barely hurts. A keeps the oracular fortune voice — "the stars say" — then twists "windfall" into your own deposit coming back as a margin call: the loss and the cosmic promise in one clean reversal. That double meaning is the fresher turn, and it reads whole in one breath.

Verdict: A. Margin: 2.
call2_BA.reasoning_tail:
Evaluate.

A: "The stars say a windfall is coming — it is your own deposit, returning as a margin call." Fortune voice (stars/oracular), twist: windfall = own deposit as margin call. About liquidation, trader loss. Funny, rueful. 17 words.

B: "Your horoscope says: hold. Your portfolio says: sold. The cookie says: order takeout." Triple structure, loss included, cookie voice, joke lands on takeout (broke). Also fresh-ish but the structure is a bit listy; "sold" at a loss is implied. Both good.

Criterion 4: freshness — A's double meaning (windfall returning as margin call) is a sharper turn. B's last word "takeout" is a decent pivot but the format is a common triple-rhythm. A reads more like a real fortune with oracular voice then punchline. A wins on 4 and 5. Margin maybe 2.
